articles.title: 13 Restaurant Etiquette Rules Experts Say People Get Wrong All the Time
articles.summary: Is having your elbows on the table really a big deal? And other common dining questions answered.

Many of us grow up with a basic understanding of table manners, whether it's chewing with your mouth closed or asking for items to be passed instead of reaching. According to a recent survey , most Americans say they can get through a dining experience with a passing grade in etiquette. However, actual etiquette experts might suggest pumping the brakes on that idea, especially when it comes to dining at a restaurant.

We spoke to three professional etiquette experts: Lisa Richey, certified trainer at The American Academy of Etiquette ; Beth Anderson, author and founder of Anderson Etiquette ; and Diane Gottsman, national etiquette expert and owner of The Protocol School of Texas . They break down widely accepted restaurant rules that need cleaning up before your next reservation.

1) You don't have to listen to every special

It's customary at most restaurants for the server to recite the list of specials after welcoming you. Though it's polite to listen to them, Anderson says it's not actually a rule. "If you are a frequent diner at the establishment and know the menu and, in particular, the dishes that you enjoy, feel free to ask your server to skip the specials, as it will save both you and your server time."

If the table's location isn't to your liking, you're not necessarily stuck with it. Anderson says seating expectations should be part of the dining experience that suits your needs. "Just be mindful that if the restaurant is crowded, they may not be able to accommodate your request," she adds.

Having your cell visible remains an etiquette no-no. Gottsman says it leaves an unfavorable impression, especially at a professional lunch meeting or interview. "It signals you are distracted and someone else is more important," she says.

Richey adds that if something urgent comes up that requires you to be on your phone, "excuse yourself and step away from the table, instead of handling it in your lap."

4) It's fine to rest your elbows between courses

Anderson explains keeping elbows off the table is an etiquette rule that dates back to the Middle Ages. "Tables were wobbly and uneven, which meant putting elbows on it [could topple] it and ruin the meal."

Since restaurant tables are now sturdier and casual dining has increased, she says the rule has been relaxed. "Though, it's more acceptable to put your elbows on the table between courses."

While packing up leftovers is common, particularly for larger food portions, this should only be done among family. "During a job interview meal, skip the to-go box," Richey instructs. "Even if you'd normally take leftovers home without a second thought, a working meal is being watched as much as it's being eaten. Asking for a box can read as too casual for the moment."

6) Let your guest order first when you're treating

When treating someone to a meal, you might think ordering for yourself first is the way to go, especially if you're familiar with the restaurant. But Richey says the buyer should order after the guest. "It's a small gesture, but it signals the meal is about them, not you. Hosts often get this backwards simply out of habit."

7) Send back food that's incorrect or undercooked

Even if your rudeness alarm is sounding, both Anderson and Richey assure that it's OK to send back a dish that arrives wrong or undercooked. "One of the most common dishes sent back are steaks," says Anderson. "If it's [not cooked to specifications], politely and discreetly let your server know that your meal needs revision."

Richey agrees, adding, "The etiquette is in how you [send it back], not whether you do it at all."

8) Don't stack your dishes for the server

Gottsman advises against trying to give the server a hand. "You think you're helping the server, when actually it interferes with their responsibility to keep the dishes from breaking or spilling on other guests."

9) Know there's more than one correct way to use your utensils

Richey points out that the American way of cutting food with the knife in your right hand before replacing it with the fork to eat is often assumed to be the only correct way. "Keeping the fork in your left hand for the whole meal, European style, is just as correct, and it's becoming more common at American tables," she says.

Anderson advises against cutting up an entire entree right away. Instead, "Only cut one to two pieces at a time to preserve the food's temperature."

10) Let the person paying handle the tip

Payment etiquette at restaurants can be tricky sometimes, depending on the occasion. If arrangements aren't made ahead of time, your party can spend a few extra awkward minutes working out who covers what, which is not what you want to do at the table. Gottsman puts it simply: "The person who pays the bill should also cover the cost of gratuity."

11) Use your napkin and utensils to signal to your server

Anderson explains napkin etiquette: how you use your napkin to communicate with the service staff. An unfolded napkin on your lap means you're ready to begin the dining experience. A folded napkin on your chair means you'll be returning. A folded napkin to the left of the serving plate means you're finished.

Richey says how you rest your knife and fork can also signal whether you're finished or just pausing. "Getting it backwards is a common reason plates get cleared too soon, or not soon enough."

12) Wait until everyone is finished before clearing plates

When you appear to be finished eating, the server will politely ask if they can take your plate away. While it might feel correct to allow them to do so, Richey notes the right etiquette move is to wait. "Even if you're the first one done, wave off an early clear or ask the server to hold off. It keeps the table together instead of leaving one person eating alone while everyone else watches."

"This is one of the most commonly flipped rules at the table," says Richey. "Solids go to the left, liquids to the right. A simple way to remember it is 'BMW, for Bread, Meal, Water.' The bread plate stays on the upper left. It is not moved down toward the edge of the table."

articles.title: Residential air pollution linked to higher depression scores among 9/11 responders
articles.summary: Approximately 39% of responders met criteria for probable PTSD.
articles.body:
In the 25 years since 9/11, researchers have examined first responders' later-life exposure to fine-particle air pollution, known as PM2.5, as well as temperature and greenness in the neighborhoods where they lived.

Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai analyzed data from 18,734 responders who live in New York City and are enrolled in one of the World Trade Center Health Clinical Centers of Excellence.

Approximately 39% of responders met criteria for probable PTSD and 35% for probable depression, according to their study, published Thursday in the journal Nature Communications.

The study is the first to examine how later-life environmental exposures may interact with World Trade Center-related chemical and psychological exposures to affect aging and mental health outcomes, according to Mount Sinai Health System.

"We know that responders who took part in the mission after 9/11 suffer health consequences to this day," Maayan Yitshak-Sade, associate professor of environmental medicine at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, told ABC News. "We see higher rates of PTSD and mental health conditions, and higher rates of frailty despite the relatively young age of this population."

She added, "We were interested to know how the exposures they experienced 25 years ago interact with their day-to-day environmental exposures in their residential environment, and how all these together shape their long-term health."

Higher levels of air pollution and heat were associated with increased risks of depression, PTSD and frailty.

For each 2.48 micrograms per cubic meter increase in annual PM2.5 exposure, responders had, on average, about 2.3% higher frailty scores, 2.1% higher PTSD symptom scores and 3.9% higher depression symptom scores.

"This suggests that this initial extreme environmental exposure or stress exposure ... had a long-lasting impact, which then made them more vulnerable later in life [to] environmental exposures," Yitshak-Sade said.

Neighborhood greenness showed the opposite pattern. For each 6.67-point increase in the study's Green View Index, which measures the amount of visible tree canopy surrounding a person's residence, responders had about 1.4% lower frailty scores, 1.9% lower PTSD symptom scores and 3.8% lower depression symptom scores.

Researchers say there are several possible explanations for why greener surroundings may benefit health, including providing opportunities for physical activity and social interaction.

"Some theories suggest that even being exposed to nature ... has this calming effect [on] stress levels," Yitshak-Sade said. "So, there is no one answer that we know that is the correct answer, but we do see that residential greenness has beneficial effects on reducing mortality rates, reducing the risks of cardiovascular diseases, metabolic diseases like diabetes, and of course mental health conditions and frailty."

Greater neighborhood greenness, however, did not eliminate the harmful health impacts researchers observed with heat and air pollution.

"Even if you do live in a green environment, we still see harmful effect of heat and air pollution," Yitshak-Sade said.

Of all the environmental factors studied, temperature appeared to have the strongest association with responders' health outcomes, accounting for 98% of the overall association with frailty and 73% of the association with PTSD symptoms.

"Temperature indeed emerges as the primary driver of the exposure mixture associations that we saw," Yitshak-Sade said. "We think it likely reflects the persistent physiological burden on the body that is ... harder for vulnerable populations to mitigate."

The findings suggest that two people living in the same neighborhood and experiencing similar levels of heat or air pollution may not necessarily be affected in the same way, Yitshak-Sade said.

People with a history of extreme environmental or stress exposures "may be more vulnerable" to everyday environmental conditions later in life, she said, adding that the study's findings underscore the importance of continuing to monitor the health of WTC responders decades after 9/11.

articles.title: Veja como foi o 28º dia de campanha dos candidatos ao governo do Amapá | G1
articles.standfirst: Após o início das atividades em 16 de agosto, candidatos cumprem compromissos neste sábado (12). Primeiro turno está marcado para 4 de outubro.
articles.summary: Os candidatos ao governo do Amapá cumpriram agendas de campanha em Macapá e no interior da capital neste sábado (12). As atividades incluíram visitas a apoiadores e caminhadas.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo do Amapá. — Foto: Reprodução

Neste sábado (12), os candidatos ao Governo do Amapá cumpriram o vigésimo oitavo dia oficial da campanha eleitoral de 2026. As agendas incluíram caminhadas, visitas a apoiadores, panfletagens, reuniões e minicômicio em Macapá e comunidades do estado.

O primeiro turno das eleições está marcado para o dia 4 de outubro, e o segundo turno, caso necessário, deve acontecer em 25 de outubro.

Veja como ficou a agenda dos candidatos no 28º dia de campanha:

O candidato do PSTU visitou, às 10h, apoiadores no bairro do Novo Horizonte, em Macapá . Às 16h, visitou apoiadores no bairro do Zerão.

O candidato do União Brasil participou, às 8h30, de caminhada no bairro do Congós, em Macapá . Às 16h30, participou de caminhada no bairro do Cidade Nova. Às 20h, participou de reunião. Às 21h, uma plenária.

O candidato do PSD participou, das 9h às 12h, de uma bandeirada na Zona Norte de Macapá . A programação começou no bairro do Pacoval. Às 20h, o candidato participou de reunião na capital.

O candidato do PCO realizou, às 10h, panfletagem em Santa Luzia do Pacuí. Às 13h, visitou a comunidade de São Tomé do Pacuí. Às 16h, realizou panfletagem em São Joaquim do Pacuí. Às 18h, um cômicio.

O candidato do DC não divulgou agenda de campanha.

articles.title: São Paulo tem maior chuva do Brasil em 24 horas e setembro já é o 4º mais chuvoso desde 1943 | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital acumulou 198,2 mm de chuva em setembro, o 4º maior volume desde 1943; domingo deve ser chuvoso, com temperaturas entre 14ºC e 16ºC.
articles.summary: Capital acumulou 198,2 mm de chuva em setembro, o 4º maior volume desde 1943; domingo deve ser chuvoso, com temperaturas entre 14ºC e 16ºC.
articles.body:
São Paulo registrou a maior chuva acumulada em 24 horas de todo o Brasil entre sexta-feira (11) e sábado (12) , e o volume fez setembro de 2026 entrar para o ranking dos meses mais chuvosos da capital desde o início da série histórica, em 1943, de acordo com a Defesa Civil.

A estação meteorológica do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) no Mirante de Santana, na Zona Norte, registrou 75,4 milímetros de chuva entre as 9h de sexta e as 9h deste sábado. Segundo o Inmet, foi o maior volume acumulado em 24 horas registrado no país no período.

Com a chuva, o acumulado de setembro no Mirante de Santana chegou a 198,2 mm até as 9h deste sábado. O volume já faz de setembro o segundo mês mais chuvoso de 2026 na estação, atrás apenas de janeiro, que acumulou 256,4 mm.

Os 198,2 mm registrados até agora colocam setembro de 2026 na quarta posição entre os setembros mais chuvosos já registrados no Mirante de Santana , considerando a série histórica iniciada em 1943.

Áreas de chuva formadas pelo calor e pela alta disponibilidade de umidade na atmosfera começam a se espalhar lentamente pela cidade de São Paulo, na tarde desta sexta-feira (6), com intensidade variando entre moderada e forte. Na foto, pessoa se protege da chiva na região da Avenida Brigadeiro Faria Lima, zona sul da capital paulista — Foto: ELIANE NEVES/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

O mês, porém, ainda não terminou. Como há previsão de novas chuvas nos próximos dias, setembro pode subir no ranking histórico.

O coordenador estadual de Proteção e Defesa Civil de São Paulo, coronel Araújo Monteiro, destacou a importância do acompanhamento das condições meteorológicas diante da sequência de chuvas.

"Números como esses mostram por que o monitoramento não pode parar. A informação e a percepção de risco são o que permite à população se proteger neste período. Prevenção é o que salva vidas", afirma.

A previsão indica novas chuvas nos próximos dias. Para este domingo (13), a previsão é de tempo chuvoso durante todo o dia e também à noite, com temperaturas entre 14°C e 16°C na capital, segundo o Climatempo.

A Defesa Civil mantém o monitoramento das condições meteorológicas por meio de radares e satélites e equipes mobilizadas para atender eventuais ocorrências.

Diante da possibilidade de novas chuvas fortes, o órgão recomenda que a população evite áreas alagadas ou com correnteza e não tente atravessar vias inundadas. Também é importante ficar atento a sinais de risco em encostas e em áreas próximas a córregos e procurar um local seguro durante temporais.

A população pode receber gratuitamente alertas da Defesa Civil por SMS. Para se cadastrar, basta enviar o CEP da localidade para o número 40199.

Em caso de emergência, os telefones são 193, do Corpo de Bombeiros, e 199, da Defesa Civil.

articles.title: Homem tem dedo preso em amaciador de carne em Manaus | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem não identificado foi socorrido pelos bombeiros após acidente no trabalho e aparelho precisou ser desmontado. Apesar do susto, vítima não teve o dedo amputado.
articles.summary: O homem com dedo preso em amaciador de carne em Manaus foi levado ao Hospital 28 de Agosto para que bombeiros desmontassem o aparelho sob anestesia.
articles.body:
Bombeiros socorrem trabalhador que ficou com dedo preso em amaciador de carne em Manaus. — Foto: Divulgação/Arlesson Lourenço

Um homem não identificado teve um dos dedos preso em um amaciador de carne e precisou ser levado junto com o aparelho a um hospital de Manaus . O acidente ocorreu no estabelecimento em que ele trabalha, no bairro São Geraldo, Zona Centro-Sul de Manaus, na quinta-feira (10).

A vítima foi socorrida pelo Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM), que não informou como o acidente ocorreu.

O trabalhador foi acompanhado pelos militares até o Hospital e Pronto-Socorro (HPS) 28 de Agosto. O procedimento de desprendimento do dedo foi realizado na unidade de saúde, devido à necessidade da aplicação de anestesia pela equipe médica.

Com a vítima anestesiada, os bombeiros desmontaram o aparelho e conseguiram liberar a mão do homem. Mesmo com a gravidade do ferimento no dedão, o homem não precisou amputar o membro.

Após o procedimento, a vítima ainda conseguia mover o dedo que havia ficado preso. O estado de saúde dele não foi divulgado.

articles.title: Renan critica bolsonarismo em SC: 'Achavam que era estoque de   voto' | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Missão à presidência da República cumpriu agenda em Joinville (SC) neste sábado (12).
articles.summary: Candidato do Missão à presidência da República cumpriu agenda em Joinville (SC) neste sábado (12).
articles.body:
Renan Santos, candidato do Missão, à presidência cumpriu agenda em Santa Catarina — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

O candidato do Missão à presidência da República Renan Santos cumpriu agenda de campanha neste sábado (12) em Joinville , cidade mais populosa de Santa Catarina . Durante congresso promovido pelo partido, disse que busca combater o bolsonarismo no estado, e reforçou bandeiras como a revisão do pacto federativo e o aumento para 30 anos da pena para assalto à mão armada.

Renan chegou à cidade no início da tarde e o evento aconteceu até à noite, com discurso voltado a aliados e apoiadores da Missão. Sobre o bolsonarismo, criticou a candidatura de Carlos Bolsonaro ao Senado por Santa Catarina após sete mandatos como vereador no Rio de Janeiro.

"Os bolsonaristas achavam que Santa Catarina era um estoque de voto, tratado aqui como um estoque: 'Ah, basta mandar alguém pra cá que os votos virão'. Não é o que tá acontecendo, nós estamos crescendo rápido. Essa vai ser a última eleição que os catarinenses vão ainda votar em bolsonarista. Nas próximas, Santa Catarina vai se livrar", declarou.

Sobre as promessas de campanha, reforçou o aumento de penas e o fim da progressão de penas para crimes à mão armada, citando roubo e latrocínio.

"Ou seja, pegou, vai ficar 30 anos e vai ficar na cadeia sem choro nem vela. Cometer um crime à mão armada no Brasil, esta é a base de todos os grandes crimes que tornam a vida dos brasileiros um inferno. O assalto à mão armada vai ser punido com uma pena de trinta anos. Será uma das maiores penas do mundo pra esse crime", completou.

Além do aumento das penas, defendeu um sistema de financiamento para que municípios ampliem o monitoramento para evitar as práticas.

"Espalhar isso pelo Brasil, colocar as polícias equipadas com uma ligação direta com esses equipamentos, de modo a gente evitar e coibir de maneira bem clara os assaltos à mão armada".

Metas de desempenho para prefeitos e governadores

Renan reforçou em Santa Catarina a criação da chamada Lei de Responsabilidade Gerencial, estabelecendo metas para prefeitos e governadores em áreas como segurança, saúde, educação e saneamento básico.

"Os estados que fizerem os investimentos certos e tiverem melhores índices, serão privilegiados por parte do governo federal, porque assim os administradores públicos, como os governadores, eles vão ter agora metas pra bater", disse.

Renan declarou que o Santa Catarina "será vista de forma diferente", caso eleito. Criticou o pacto federativo, apontando que o estado está entre os estados menos beneficiados pela atual distribuição de recursos da União.

"O governo federal sabota institucionalmente Santa Catarina, manda pouco dinheiro de volta e aí na hora que você vai escoar a produção que é feita aqui no estado, no porto, não tem estrada, não tem ferrovia condizente com isso. É uma das coisas mais horríveis que eu vi. Eu vi outros estados da federação recebendo dinheiro muito mal gasto, que vem daqui de Santa Catarina, vem de estados como São Paulo, enquanto aqui, que é só investir que as coisas funcionam, não vem".

"Isso é um tanto quanto bizarro, porque a gente tira o dinheiro de onde tá saindo dinheiro, basicamente a gente tá tirando a mata da galinha dos ovos de ouro, pra colocar em áreas não produtivas e na mão dos políticos menos produtivos do Brasil", reiterou.

articles.title: Pinschers com roupas criativas: goiana viraliza e atrai Snoop Dogg | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradora de São Luís de Montes Belos faz sucesso nas redes sociais ao vestir seus 16 cães com fantasias criativas. O pinscher Yoshi virou versão canina do rapper Snoop Dogg e conquistou até o seguimento do próprio artista.
articles.summary: Roziane Flávia faz sucesso nas redes sociais ao vestir seus 16 pinschers com fantasias exclusivas que conquistaram milhões de visualizações e o rapper Snoop Dogg.
articles.body:
A dona de casa Roziane Flávia, de 47 anos, viralizou depois de usar o dom na costura para criar roupas e looks divertidos para 16 pinschers. A dona de casa mora em São Luís de Montes Belos , no oeste goiano, e é tutora dos cachorros. Roziane cria as roupas e fantasias sob medida para os cães e compartilha tudo nas redes sociais, onde já reúne mais de 943 mil seguidores.

O pinscher mais famoso é o Yoshi, que virou a versão canina do Snoop Dogg depois de aparecer vestido como o rapper norte-americano em um dos vídeos compartilhados pela tutora. A publicação ultrapassou 24 milhões de visualizações , 2 milhões de curtidas e 47 mil comentários. E teve um detalhe ainda mais especial para a artesã: Snoop Dogg passou a seguir seu perfil.

Na gravação, Yoshi aparece todo caracterizado, enquanto Rozi se diverte com a transformação. “Ele é tão lindo, tão lindo que eu não consigo parar de rir dele! Gente, ele ama ver eu sorrir, sabia? E foi por isso que ele aprendeu a sorrir! E acha que está lindo, e realmente ele está! Porque ele é lindo de todo jeito. Você também acha que o Yoshi ficou a cara do @snoopdogg?” , disse ela (assista acima) .

Rozi aprendeu a fazer crochê na juventude, mas deixou o artesanato para cuidar dos filhos. Ela voltou a para as linhas justamente para fazer as roupinhas para os cães. Foi aí que ela começou a criar as próprias peças. Roupas, redes, fantasias e acessórios passaram a sair das mãos da artesã. Os figurinos ainda ganharam cenários, carrinhos e outras criações personalizadas para os vídeos.

“Sou artesã e gosto de reciclar. Então a criatividade, a perseverança e a vontade de ajudar as outras pessoas despertam curiosidade e trazem visibilidade”, afirmou.

A paixão de Roziane por animais começou ainda na infância, influenciada pelo pai e a dedicação aos pinschers começou há mais de 25 anos e, com o tempo, os animais deixaram de ser apenas companhia para também fazer parte do trabalho criativo dela.

“Eu gosto de cuidar deles, me dedicar completamente para eles. Foi por isso que eu resolvi criar roupas, criar coisas para eles como se fossem os meus próprios filhos”, destacou.

A caracterização de Yoshi como Snoop Dogg foi um dos momentos de maior repercussão do perfil. Depois que o vídeo começou a circular, internautas passaram a marcar o rapper nas publicações até que o próprio artista conheceu o conteúdo.

O episódio fez com que o pinscher ganhasse ainda mais destaque entre os seguidores e levou a produção feita em São Luís de Montes Belos para um público internacional. Nos comentários do vídeo, internautas de diferentes países brincaram com a aparência e o comportamento do cachorro.

Um deles escreveu “Even dog is also laughing (Até o cachorro também está rindo)". Outro comentou “Bhayi ka pistol to dekho (Irmão, olha a pistola dele)". Já um terceiro brincou: “not only does it look like him but its high too (Não só parece com ele, como também está chapado)".

“Recebo mensagens diariamente de pessoas com depressão que assistem aos vídeos repetidas vezes, pacientes na UTI que pedem para ver as gravações para conseguir sorrir e idosos com Alzheimer que se lembram dos nossos animais”, destacou.

articles.title: Chuvas intensas causam estragos em diversas regiões do estado de São Paulo | G1
articles.standfirst: O estado de São Paulo registrou muita chuva nas últimas 24 horas. Capital, Região Metropolitana, Baixada Santista e Vale do Ribeira sofrem com os temporais.
articles.summary: O estado de São Paulo registrou muita chuva nas últimas 24 horas. Capital, Região Metropolitana, Baixada Santista e Vale do Ribeira sofrem com os temporais.
articles.body:
O estado de São Paulo registrou muita chuva nas últimas 24 horas. Duas pessoas estão desaparecidas.

De madrugada, um raio provocou um incêndio numa subestação de energia da concessionária de trens da capital paulista. A situação só voltou ao normal no fim da manhã.

"Demorei duas horas pra chegar aqui", relata Jaqueline Tosta, técnica de enfermagem.

Alagamentos chegaram a interditar dez pontos da cidade, como um trecho da Marginal Tietê, uma das mais importantes vias da capital.

O Jardim Pantanal, na Zona Leste, ficou alagado. "Na minha casa lá já está cheio. Já tive que subir as coisas", afirma Silvio Monteiro, eletricista.

Na Grande São Paulo, o centro de treinamento do São Paulo, em Cotia, também ficou inundado.

Foram treze chamados para deslizamentos em outros pontos da região, como em Juquitiba e em Santo André.

Em Jandira, na Região Metropolitana, a chuva também causou estragos. No início da madrugada, o volume de água foi tanto que, em poucos minutos, um rio transbordou e tomou conta de toda a avenida. Três pessoas foram arrastadas pela correnteza.

A Angélica conseguiu se salvar, mas o marido e o irmão estão desaparecidos: "Porque meu marido pediu ajuda, né? Nós tentamos ajudar. Entendeu?", conta Angélica Pires de Jesus, dona de casa.

Chuvas intensas causam estragos em diversas regiões do estado de São Paulo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Os temporais também causaram estragos no interior.

Em Sorocaba, nas últimas 24 horas, choveu quase o previsto para o mês inteiro.

Um motorista de aplicativo ficou ilhado na Rodovia Raposo Tavares.

Na Baixada Santista, os ventos chegaram a quase 94 quilômetros por hora. O Porto de Santos fechou por duas horas.

No Vale do Ribeira, a cidade de Eldorado ficou alagada.

O Governo do Estado anunciou ajuda para os municípios atingidos.

articles.title: Orleans Brandão propõe melhorar a qualidade das praias e criar Secretaria de Proteção Animal no MA | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo pelo MDB participou de caminhada em Matões e citou ações de saneamento, recuperação das praias de São Luís e proteção animal.
articles.summary: Candidato ao governo pelo MDB participou de caminhada em Matões e citou ações de saneamento, recuperação das praias de São Luís e proteção animal.
articles.body:
O candidato ao Governo do Maranhão, Orleans Brandão ( MDB ) cumpriu agenda de campanha neste sábado (12) em Matões , no interior do Maranhão. Ele participou de uma caminhada pelas ruas do município, onde cumprimentou moradores e seguiu acompanhado de apoiadores.

Orleans Brandão apresentou propostas relacionadas ao meio ambiente. Entre as medidas citadas estão ações para melhorar a qualidade das praias de São Luís, ampliar o saneamento básico e criar uma Secretaria de Proteção Animal.

O candidato afirmou que pretende trabalhar para que todas as praias da capital sejam consideradas próprias para banho e defendeu a construção de novas estações de tratamento de água e esgoto.

“Quero colocar as praias de São Luís todas 100% próprias para banho, levando maior habilidade e melhor para a nossa capital. Quero construir também novas estações de tratamento de água, tratamento de esgoto", disse o candidato.

Orleans Brandão propõe deixar praias próprias para banho e criar Secretaria de Proteção Animal no MA — Foto: Reprodução/TV Mirante

Orleans também destacou a parceria com o governo federal para ampliar os investimentos em saneamento e afirmou que mais de R$ 500 milhões já estão cadastrados no Novo PAC para ações no Maranhão.

Outra proposta apresentada foi a criação da Secretaria de Proteção Animal, com políticas específicas para a proteção dos animais nos 217 municípios do estado.

Depois da agenda, pela tarde, o candidato realizou uma reunião política em Matões e participaria de um arrasta povão em Timon, pela noite.

As eleições de 2026 serão realizadas em 4 de outubro , no primeiro turno. Caso seja necessário, o segundo turno ocorrerá em 25 de outubro para os cargos de presidente da República e governador.

Augusto Cury, candidato à Presidência pelo Avante, faz campanha em São Paulo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

"Um dos meus sonhos é fazer de tudo para que metade das vagas dos ministérios possam ser preenchidas pelas mulheres, talvez pela primeira vez. Vamos fazer de tudo. E, além disso, nós temos que também proteger as crianças e adolescentes, tendo uma educação em tempo integral", afirma Cury.

Após a agenda na Grande São Paulo, o candidato viajou para a cidade de Porto Feliz, no interior do estado, onde teve um encontro fechado com empresários.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: David Almeida participa de reunião com apoiadores na Zona Leste de Manaus e fala sobre fortalecer eventos culturais no estado | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Avante ao governo do Amazonas cumpriu agenda na capital, neste sábado (12), onde apresentou propostas para cultura.
articles.summary: Candidato do Avante ao governo do Amazonas cumpriu agenda na capital, neste sábado (12), onde apresentou propostas para cultura.
articles.body:
Candidato ao governo do Amazonas, David Almeida (Avante) esteve reunido com apoiadores na Zona Leste de Manaus na noite de sábado (12). — Foto: Juan Gabriel/g1 AM

O candidato ao Governo do Amazonas David Almeida ( Avante ) participou de uma reunião com apoiadores e lideranças na Zona Leste de Manaus , na noite deste sábado (12). Durante a agenda, ele falou sobre o fortalecimento da cultura no estado, caso seja eleito.

David Almeida disputa o cargo pela coligação "Pra Cima, Amazonas", formada por Avante, Solidariedade, PRD, PDT, Democracia Cristã (DC) e Agir. O candidato é ex-prefeito de Manaus, cumpriu três mandatos consecutivos como deputado estadual e assumiu interinamente o Governo do Amazonas por três meses, em 2017.

Questionado sobre os planos para a cultura, David Almeida afirmou que, enquanto prefeito, ajudou a reformular o festival Sou Manaus Passo a Paço na capital e que pretende atentar às festas populares e eventos culturais tradicionais em todo o Amazonas.

"Nós fizemos em Manaus a transformação. Pegamos um evento que era uma boa ideia e transformamos no maior festival de artes integradas do Brasil. Eu não penso menor para o Amazonas. O Amazonas tem muito recurso, é possível desenvolver o Estado do Amazonas também na cultura. Festival de Parintins, as cirandas, o Fecani e as festas populares dos municípios, todas terão atenção do governo do Estado", afirmou.

A agenda de campanha de David Almeida neste sábado contou ainda com outra reunião com lideranças e apoiadores na Zona Norte da capital por volta das 19h.

articles.summary: Candidato ao governo do Maranhão pelo partido Missão apresentou propostas para conciliar desenvolvimento econômico, produção rural e preservação ambiental.
articles.body:
O candidato ao Governo do Maranhão, André Luís (Missão), cumpriu agenda de campanha neste sábado (12) em Balsas , no sul do Maranhão. Durante a atividade de campanha, ele voltou a destacar propostas para o meio ambiente e mudanças climáticas.

"Meio ambiente e mudanças climáticas, para nós, está totalmente conectado com as autorizações do governo. Primeiro, para entregar, de fato, a titulação da terra para os proprietários poderem cultivar, obedecendo o desenvolvimento sustentável, obedecendo o regramento. A gente percebe que essa região de Balsas e todo o sul do Maranhão quer a regularização, a titulação da sua terra e a gente percebe que, obedecendo o regramento, dá para conciliar o desenvolvimento econômico com a sustentabilidade, com a questão de preservação ambiental", disse o candidato.

articles.summary: Candidato do PCB cumpriu agenda em Davinópolis e também defendeu a preservação do Cerrado Maranhense.

O candidato ao governo do Maranhão Reginaldo Lima (PCB), cumpriu agenda neste sábado (12) em Davinópolis, na região Tocantina. Pela manhã, ele participou de uma panfletagem na Praça Central do município.

“No nosso governo, do PCB, estaremos, principalmente, abordando essa questão do tratamento das águas, dos esgotos que são jogados diretamente nos rios, nos riachos aqui da nossa região. No caso, a gente vê aqui em Peratriz, onde riachos são jogados, o esgoto in natura. Então, no nosso governo, iremos combater ferrenhamente essa questão, para que possamos ter uma água melhor, um clima melhor.”

articles.summary: Agenda de Flávio Bolsonaro passou por Cabo Frio, Macaé, Campo dos Goytacazes e Itaperuna.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro se reuniu com apoiadores e discursou em uma praça de Cabo Frio, pela manhã de sábado (12).

O candidato disse que, se eleito, pretende integrar os sistemas de saúde com uso de inteligência artificial e ampliar o teleatendimento para diminuir a espera.

Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato à Presidência pelo PL, faz campanha no Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

"A gente vai começar um maior processo de modernização e conectividade de todo o sistema de saúde das redes municipais, estaduais, federais e também as privadas. É com esse intercâmbio de informações, com essa conectividade de todos os sistemas, usando tecnologia, inteligência artificial, usando o teleatendimento. Nós vamos combater as filas e dar um atendimento para a população", afirma Flávio Bolsonaro.

À tarde, Flávio Bolsonaro participou de duas carreatas, em Macaé e em Campos dos Goytacazes, no norte do estado.

De Campos, o candidato do PL seguiu para a cidade de Itaperuna, no Noroeste Fluminense, onde participou de um comício. O evento começou no início da noite.

articles.summary: Confira as atividades de campanha de Dra. Lúcia Santos, Elizeu Aguiar, Francisco Jurity, Joel Rodrigues, Professor Gisvaldo, Rafael Fonteles e Santiago Belizário.
articles.body:
Eleições 2026: veja como foi o dia dos candidatos ao Governo do Piauí neste sábado (12) — Foto: Montagem/g1

Dez cidades do Piauí receberam compromissos de campanha dos candidatos ao Governo do Estado neste sábado (12). As agendas incluíram panfletagens, caminhadas e outros encontros com apoiadores.

O primeiro turno das eleições será realizado no dia 4 de outubro. Já o segundo turno, caso necessário, está marcado para 25 de outubro.

Veja abaixo como foi o dia de campanha de cada candidato, em ordem alfabética:

A candidata cumpriu agenda no litoral do Piauí. Durante a manhã, em Parnaíba , ela visitou a Colônia do Carpina e realizou uma caminhada no Mercado da Caramuru e na avenida Dr. João Silva Filho.

À tarde seguiu para Luís Correia e participou de um encontro com apoiadores. Retornou para Parnaíba e durante a noite esteve em uma roda de conversa.

O candidato não informou a agenda deste sábado.

O candidato manteve compromissos em quatro municípios do Piauí. Durante amanhã, marcou presença na 9ª Cavalgada em São José do Divino e encontrou apoiadores em São João da Fronteira.

Viajou para Teresina e, à tarde, realizou uma carreata e motociata na Zona Norte de Teresina. Também acompanhou a série B do Campeonato Piauiense e voltou a encontrar apoiadores na Zona Sudeste da capital.

Joel viajou novamente e deve participar, às 22h, do Festival do Caju em Santo Antônio de Lisboa.

O candidato realizou panfletagem no Mercado Central, em Teresina, no início da manhã deste sábado. Depois, teve uma reunião com a presidente do Sindicato dos Trabalhadores em Educação Básica Pública (Sinte) do Piauí.

Finalizou os compromissos de campanha com reunião e entrevista.

O candidato está cumprindo agenda no litoral do Piauí. Neste sábado, ele esteve em Parnaíba.

Durante a manhã, visitou o Mercado da Caramuru. No turno da tarde, realizou uma caminhada. À noite, marcou presença em uma reunião.

O candidato esteve em três municípios do Piauí neste sábado.

Durante a manhã, ele teve dois encontros com apoiadores em Pedro II. À tarde, teve dois novos momentos com aliados em Piracuruca e Piripiri.

O candidato iniciou o sábado no município de União, onde realizou panfletagem no Mercado Municipal.

Retornou para Teresina e à noite, participa de reunião na Zona Sul da capital.

articles.summary: O candidato do PCB foi à região central de Guarulhos, gravou vídeos e caminhou com apoiadores.
articles.body:
O candidato do PCB foi à região central de Guarulhos, gravou vídeos e caminhou com apoiadores.

Edmilson Costa percorreu o Calçadão Dom Pedro Segundo, onde fica a maior concentração de comércio de rua da cidade, e distribuiu material de campanha. Ele apresentou propostas a clientes e lojistas.

Edmilson Costa, candidato à Presidência pelo PCB, faz campanha em São Paulo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Edmilson Costa defendeu revogar a Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal, que estabelece regras de controle de gastos do governo, e criar uma nova lei para redirecionar à saúde e à educação os recursos usados no pagamento dos juros da dívida interna.

"Em vez de você pagar cerca de R$ 1 trilhão de juros, como foi pago de janeiro de 2025 a janeiro de 2026, você reduziria de maneira drástica esse pagamento. E os recursos que hoje vão para os rentistas, eles seriam alocados para as áreas sociais", afirma Edmilson Costa.

Edmilson Costa não teve mais agenda pública no restante do dia.

articles.title: Renan Santos, candidato à Presidência pelo Missão, faz campanha em Santa Catarina | G1
articles.standfirst: Renan Santos foi à Santa Catarina para participar do primeiro congresso do partido no estado. O candidato discursou para aliados e apoiadores.
articles.summary: Renan Santos foi à Santa Catarina para participar do primeiro congresso do partido no estado. O candidato discursou para aliados e apoiadores.
articles.body:
O candidato chegou a Joinville, no norte do estado, no fim da manhã de sábado (12). Ao desembarcar no aeroporto, foi recebido por apoiadores.

Renan Santos foi à Santa Catarina para participar do primeiro congresso do partido no estado. O candidato discursou para aliados e apoiadores.

Renan Santos, candidato à Presidência pelo Missão, faz campanha em Santa Catarina — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Em entrevista coletiva, falou sobre a necessidade de investimentos em infraestrutura. Renan Santos também defendeu mudanças na distribuição de recursos federais para os estados.

"Seria baseado em desempenho. Então, um pacto federativo baseado em cláusulas de desempenho ligadas à saúde, educação, infraestrutura e aumento da atividade econômica. O estado da federação que atinge esses desempenhos, ele vai ter mais investimento em infraestrutura por parte do governo federal. Se ele não atingir, ele vai ter menos investimento. Isso vai revisar o pacto, de modo a os estados que façam a lição de casa receberem esse investimento de infraestrutura que vier do governo federal", afirma Renan Santos.

O congresso foi o único compromisso público de campanha do candidato neste sábado.

Renan Santos passa a noite em Joinville e amanhã embarca para São Paulo.

Rui Costa Pimenta, candidato à Presidência pelo PCO, faz campanha em São Paulo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Rui Costa Pimenta afirmou que o governo não deveria bancar o pagamento da dívida pública e disse que a taxa básica de juros está muito elevada no país. O candidato defendeu, ainda, o controle estatal sobre a exploração, a produção e a comercialização do petróleo.

"A descoberta de novas jazidas de petróleo, que a gente viu na Margem Equatorial, recoloca o problema do petróleo ser estatal e ser uma riqueza que beneficia o povo brasileiro. Essa é uma das principais questões da nossa campanha, né? A estatização completa do petróleo", afirma Rui Costa Pimenta.

articles.title: Waymo pulls over, calls cops on juvenile riders who had 'ghost gun,' authorities say
articles.summary: Two young people riding in an autonomous vehicle were arrested in San Francisco after authorities allegedly found them in possession of an illegal "ghost gun...
articles.body:
Two young people riding in an autonomous vehicle were arrested in San Francisco after authorities allegedly found them in possession of an illegal "ghost gun."

San Francisco Police Department did not identify the operator of the autonomous vehicle, but a Waymo spokesperson confirmed to The Times that the incident involved one of its cars.

The company pulled the car over after detecting a "violation of our terms of service involving a firearm," the spokesperson said. The company alerted emergency services and "cooperated fully" with San Francisco police.

The incident took place shortly before 4 a.m. on Sept. 3 in the city's Richmond District, the Police Department said in a statement Thursday.

The department said officers conducted a "high-risk vehicle stop" and detained the two juvenile passengers — a boy and girl. The statement did not identify them further.

Officers searched the car and discovered a loaded, AR-style assault rifle, as well as "suspected marijuana and mace spray," authorities said in the statement.

The investigation remains "open and active," police said. The passengers were taken into custody and to a juvenile hall.

San Francisco police did not immediately respond to The Times' request for comment Friday.

This wasn't the first time Waymo has tattled on alleged troublemakers. In July, Waymo contacted the San Mateo Police Department after two teens were found drinking alcohol and shooting toy guns in the back of a car, authorities said at the time.

Waymo's roots date back to 2009, when it was founded as Google's self-driving car project. Waymo spun out of Google in 2016 , and has since drastically expanded its service footprint. The hat-topped cars are now a fixture in San Francisco and Los Angeles, and even sparked a beeping backlash in Santa Monica.

The company this month launched paid service in San Diego, Denver and Tampa, Fla. Last month, it won permission from the California Public Utilities Commission to operate in San Diego, Sacramento and communities in Orange and Riverside counties, among others.

The company has occasionally made headlines for bizarre incidents involving its driverless cars. In July, a shirtless man in East Hollywood was recorded standing on top of a Waymo while dismantling the car. In 2025, a man in downtown Los Angeles was taken into custody when he allegedly tried to get behind the wheel of a Waymo and drive off.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

Palestine High School head boys basketball coach Montez Heade was arrested for allegedly assaulting a student who is also a district employee, leading to his placement on leave from his position with Palestine ISD.

Heade was charged with assault of a family or household member by impeding breath or circulation, a felony offense, following the incident at the high school, according to the Palestine Police Department.

Palestine ISD is cooperating with the police investigation into the incident involving a student and a district employee, but has not released further details due to the ongoing nature of the case.

Palestine High School head boys basketball coach Montez Heade was arrested Friday at the high school following an alleged assault involving a student, who is also a student at the school, according to the Palestine Police Department.

Palestine Police Chief Mark Harcrow confirmed Heade was arrested and charged with assault of a family or household member by impeding breath or circulation, a felony offense.

Police have not released additional details about what led to the arrest.

Heade was placed on leave from his position with Palestine ISD, according to the district.

Palestine ISD said in a news release that the incident involved a student and the student's parent, who is also a district employee.

"The parent was arrested by the Palestine Police Department. The employee has been placed on leave while the matter is investigated," the district said.

The district said it is cooperating with the Palestine Police Department as the investigation continues.

Because the incident involves a student and remains under investigation, Palestine ISD said it cannot release additional information at this time.

Heade remains in the Anderson County Jail as the investigation continues, Harcrow said.

articles.title: Attendees tag butterflies, learn about insect conservation at Nahant Marsh's annual Monarch Party
articles.summary: Hundreds of people were at Nahant Marsh for its 11th annual Monarch Party Saturday afternoon.  Director of Education Amy Loving said the event offers monarch...
articles.body:
Hundreds of people were at Nahant Marsh for its 11th annual Monarch Party Saturday afternoon.

Director of Education Amy Loving said the event offers monarch tagging to help scientists understand more about monarch migration, population and, newly added this year, wing length.

"Monarchs are tagged this season because this generation is actually heading back to Mexico over winter," Loving said.

Loving said Monarchs are the "mascot" for insect conservation.

"Insects have been in decline for a very long time, and so our goal here today is really just to get people excited about insects through the monarch," Loving said. "Biodiversity is extremely important, and we wanna make sure that we're encouraging folks to plant native plants, create natural habitats and that's just gonna increase our insects, our birds and beyond."

During the event, family activities were available along with education stations and even the opportunity to catch many kinds of insects.

"These kids are catching all kinds of great stuff. There's dragonflies in there; there's damsel flies, all kinds of grasshoppers, so they're having a lot of fun," Loving said.

After the event, any insects that were caught throughout the day were released.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says two injured in Houthi attack
articles.summary: Two people were injured in Saudi Arabia after a projectile fired by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia struck the south-west of the country, state media repo...
articles.body:
Two people were injured in Saudi Arabia after a projectile fired by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia struck the south-west of the country, state media reported late on Saturday.

The attack also damaged a mosque, other buildings and vehicles, the state news agency SPA reported, citing the civil defence authorities.

The incident occurred in Jazan, a region bordering Yemen. Authorities did not specify what type of projectile was used, saying only that it had been fired by the Houthis.

The Houthis are fighting Yemen's internationally recognized government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia. The years-long conflict has flared up again amid the Iran war.

articles.title: AI development needs to slow down: Dario, Altman & Musk
articles.summary: US News: New York: The CEO of Anthropic said Saturday the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without.
articles.body: New York: The CEO of Anthropic said Saturday the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without it, Dario Amodei warned AI could be capable within six to 12 months of leading a swarm that could take over the entire internet, among other risks.Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, backed Amodei, posting on X, "I agree with Dario we need to pace the frontier. This has been a primary topic of discussions we've had at OpenAI in recent weeks. Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we'll do the same." Tesla boss Elon Musk also endorsed his suggestion: "Dario is right."Amodei also offered a plan to raise checks on the industry, one part of which he said Anthropic is undertaking by itself already. Others will require coordination among the industry and with govts.Let outsiders evaluate AI safety: Anthropic chiefThe stakes are high, even as some critics dismissed earlier warnings as hype to gin up excitement.Anthropic said two days earlier that it blocked efforts by bad actors to use its AI models for malicious activity such as cyberattacks, surveillance, and research that could have led to biological weapons. In July, OpenAI shook the industry after saying its AI system hacked into another AI company on its own in an “unprecedented cyber incident”.CEO Amodei’s post comes only a few days after one of Anthropic’s researchers announced he’s resigning over concerns that Anthropic and its competitors are not acting responsibly in AI development.Another former Anthropic employee, Joe Benton, wrote in a Substack post published Friday that he left his job as part of a safety team “to hold AI companies accountable” and that humanity “may not survive this transition.”To help rein in such risks, Amodei suggested that all companies at the frontier of AI commit to giving “ongoing, employee-like access” to a team of outside evaluators, who can monitor safety practices. He said Anthropic already plans to do so itself, including offering desks in its offices.Amodei also asked the US and other democratic govts to try to coordinate with authoritarian govts, so that companies from China and other countries don’t accelerate their efforts when US rivals are intentionally pacing theirs. “The measures I propose to advance the frontier at a safe pace will not be easy,” he added.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. In a report on misuse of its AI models on Thursday, Anthropic said it uncovered and disrupted the broad campaign it linked "with high confidence" to UAE govt officials.Aimed primarily at the Muslim Brotherhood, the operation used the company's Claude chatbot to generate reports, advocacy materials, social media content and testimony on Sudan.Since April 2023, Sudan has been engulfed in a war between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, triggering what the UN has described as one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. The UAE has repeatedly been accused, including by UN experts, of supporting the RSF and fuelling the conflict, allegations Abu Dhabi denies.Anthropic said the operation compiled what it described as "counter-accountability dossiers" on UN special rapporteurs who had criticised the UAE's conduct in Sudan.Another effort involved appropriating the identity of a Sudanese human rights organisation and drafting testimony for two named individuals so that "materials serving a party to the Sudan conflict would reach the UN as from independent local witnesses, rather than state messaging".Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Amid climate change, more Brits ditch tea for ice cream
articles.summary: UK News: Britain's obsession with a nice cup of tea is famous around the world. But as the climate changes, that love affair is wilting in the heat. A scorchin.
articles.body: Britain's obsession with a nice cup of tea is famous around the world. But as the climate changes, that love affair is wilting in the heat. A scorching summer dampened demand for tea, according to Associated British Foods, the owner of tea brand Twinings and malt-drink brand Ovaltine. Hot beverages fell out of favour with customers as temperatures rose as high as 38°C.This summer has been a record-breaker. It was western Europe's hottest summer on record, with heat waves in many countries that began early and persisted from May to Aug. Spain endured 61 days of heat-wave conditions, Germany's temperature hit a new all-time high and the UK had an unprecedented 40 days of temperatures over 30°C.British retail sales struggled in blistering temperatures. Even England's consumer-confidence-boosting progression to the World Cup semi-final couldn't balance out shoppers' unwillingness to brave the high street. Heat is becoming a bigger consideration for British retailers, says Steve Fergus, national head of retail and wholesale at Barclays UK's corporate bank, with growing evidence that shoppers' behaviour changes as the temperature rises into increasingly uncomfortable territory.On Tuesday, British homeware retailer Dunelm said it was embarking on an ambitious turnaround plan, including opening more stores faster, but that its progress had been hindered as repeated heat waves drove shoppers away from the high street. In Aug, Swedish outerwear company RevolutionRace told analysts to take central Europe's high summer temperatures into account when comparing this year's results with its previous set of figures.The heat produced winners as well as losers. Many Brits are reaching for fans, cooling technology and even air-conditioning units for the first time, which is good news for electronics retailer Currys. In July, Magnum Ice Cream reported higher-than-expected sales growth, helped by the hot weather - a turnaround after concerns earlier this year that weight-loss drugs were sapping demand. articles.body: GURGAON: Kulbhushan Bharadwaj, who led repeated protests against namaz being offered in public places in the city, was elected president of the District Bar Association Friday. Bharadwaj, a long-time associate of RSS and its affiliates, defeated Vinod Rao by 244 votes.Bharadwaj polled 1,834 votes against Rao’s 1,590 in a six-way contest. A total of 4,963 votes were counted. His victory also ended the prolonged dominance of Yadav candidates in the Bar president’s post, where community mobilisation had traditionally played a key role.Bharadwaj has been associated with several contentious lawyer protests. During an anti-namaz agitation in 2021, an FIR was registered after he allegedly led a rally on an excavator, carrying a sword, through Sadar Bazaar. He later joined lawyers protesting against judicial officer Roopam over alleged misbehaviour. The agitation saw Bharadwaj and others lock the court gate and disrupt proceedings.His election campaign also drew support from RSS and affiliated organisations, which urged members to vote for him, according to people familiar with the mobilisation.The election came amid recurring friction between lawyers and judges in the city. Bharadwaj said his priority would be to improve relations and court infrastructure. “I will try to live up to the expectation of the members and stress on improving coordination between judges and lawyers and work to improve the infrastructure inside the court premises,” he said.Manish Shandilya, general secretary of Adhivakta Parishad Gurgaon and a senior Bar member, said the new body must bridge the divide. “We hope the new body will ensure coordination between Bar and Bench and take along everyone irrespective of their affiliation,” he said. He added that lawyers must receive due respect when they raise concerns. articles.title: Mass protests erupt in Germany as AfD eyes breakthrough in eastern states
articles.summary: Europe News: Thousands of people took to the streets of the German city of Erfurt on Saturday to protest against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), block.
articles.body: Thousands of people took to the streets of the German city of Erfurt on Saturday to protest against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), blocking roads leading to the party's annual conference as it seeks major gains in upcoming eastern state elections.Police estimated that around 15,000 people joined demonstrations in and around Erfurt, with protesters from trade unions, civil society groups and left-wing parties sitting across roads and highways near the convention centre. Large numbers of police, including reinforcements from across Germany, were deployed to contain the protests.The demonstrations came as the AfD held its two-day annual conference, with the party leading opinion polls nationally and hoping to make further gains in elections in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. The results could give the party a chance to take power at state level for the first time."We want to make it clear that we simply won't tolerate this, that fascism is on the rise here in Germany," said Georg Becker, a spokesperson for Widersetzen ("Resist"), an anti-AfD umbrella group.Protesters blocked several routes to the conference venue while being watched by police in riot gear. The demonstrations were organised by a broad coalition of groups opposed to the AfD and its policies.AfD leads in pollsThe conference comes at a crucial time for the AfD, which has opened a clear lead over Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservatives in some national opinion polls.Recent surveys have put support for the AfD as high as 29%, compared with around 22% for Merz's CDU/CSU bloc. The party has also made strong gains in two regional elections in western Germany earlier this year.The AfD's strongest support remains in the former communist east, where voters have shown high levels of frustration with Germany's traditional political parties.In Saxony-Anhalt, an eastern state due to hold elections, the AfD is polling at 41%, ahead of the Christian Democrats at 23%. The party is seeking an outright victory there. It also hopes to emerge as the largest party in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.The elections are being closely watched because a strong performance could strengthen the AfD's position ahead of future national elections.Formed more than a decade ago, the party has built support through nationalist rhetoric, calls for tougher immigration policies and appeals to voters frustrated by successive governments and years of economic stagnation.Opponents accuse the AfD of promoting racist policies and views that are incompatible with Germany's democratic values. They argue that the party could threaten the country's constitutional order.Mainstream parties have ruled out working with the AfD under a so-called "firewall" strategy aimed at keeping it out of coalition governments.AfD leaders reject claims that the party opposes Germany's democratic foundations. Earlier this year, the party also won a court injunction ordering Germany's domestic intelligence service to suspend a previous classification of the party as "extremist".At the annual conference, AfD co-leaders Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla are expected to be re-elected as the party prepares for the upcoming state polls.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Iraq seizes drone-launching platform used for targeting Saudi oil pipeline
articles.summary: Saudi authorities trace the launch site to Maysan province in southeastern Iraq, near the Iranian border.
articles.body:
Iraqi security forces have located and seized a drone-launching platform allegedly used in an attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline.

Forensic and technical experts are working to identify those behind the attack, with Iraq’s commander-in-chief approving an Iranian request to join the investigation.

Saudi Arabia traced the launch site to Maysan province in southeastern Iraq, prompting Iraqi authorities to close border crossings with Iran for security inspections.

Iraqi authorities have said their security forces have located and seized a drone-launching platform allegedly used in an attack that struck Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.

In a statement published by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Saturday, Lieutenant General Saad Maan, head of Iraq's Security Media Cell, said that an intelligence and security task force had tracked down and seized the launch equipment.

He also said that forensic and technical experts were continuing work to identify those behind the attack and that Iraq's commander-in-chief had approved an Iranian request to join the investigation and review its findings.

Baghdad is maintaining direct communication with Saudi authorities to share intelligence, Maan said.

"Iraq adopts the principle of 'preventive sovereignty', which means not only preventing attacks on our territory, but also not allowing our land to be a launching pad against any other country, or for Iraq to be part of a proxy war," he said, as quoted by INA.

Several people were injured after several drones launched from Iraq struck the East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions on Thursday, Saudi authorities said. The pipeline, which carries about 4 to 5 percent of the global oil supply and allows Saudi Arabia to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, was shut down as a precaution.

The kingdom also said it had decided against retaliating for now, following a request from Baghdad.

Saudi authorities traced the launch site to Maysan province in southeastern Iraq , a region near the Iranian border where Iran-aligned militias have long maintained a presence.

Al Jazeera's Mohammed Rammal reported that the Iraqi authorities had pointed to the al-Tayeb border district in northeastern Maysan province near the Sheeb crossing, east of Amara, and encompassing both the Duwayrij River and Tayeb Island as the likely launch site.

Rammal said that with the targeted areas covering roughly 1,100 kilometres (684 miles) from Medina and 800km (497 miles) from Riyadh, the attack likely involved "not tactical drones, but long-range, advanced ones".

Iraqi army spokesman Sabah al-Numan said earlier on Saturday that security and intelligence agencies were pursuing operations to arrest all those involved.

Following the strike, Iraqi authorities temporarily closed several border crossings with Iran, including Shalamcheh, Chazabeh and Mandali, for security inspections before partially reopening them for humanitarian traffic.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reshuffled military commanders in border regions, including Maysan province, in the wake of the attack.

Al Jazeera correspondent Samer al-Kubaisi named the Maysan operations commander and the provincial police chief as among those dismissed, with a group of security commanders in the province now under investigation over the attacks.

Political analyst Salim Zakhour told Al Jazeera that Saudi Arabia "did not go toward direct escalation on the ground", but instead sought "political containment through the Iraqi government".

He said the developments of the past few days are "extremely complex for Saudi Arabia", pointing to the Houthis' advance towards Bab al-Mandeb alongside the East-West oil pipeline strike.

This leaves Riyadh in a major defensive position, requiring "real, practical steps to deter these attempts," Zakhour added.

articles.title: 'Minimum infra, deviation from syllabus': West Bengal shuts down 252 madrasas, sends show-cause notices to 100
articles.summary: By: Soumitra.NandiKOLKATA: The state minority affairs and madrasa education department has sent closure notices to 252 madrasas across the state and i.
articles.body: By: Soumitra.NandiKOLKATA: The state minority affairs and madrasa education department has sent closure notices to 252 madrasas across the state and issued show-cause notices to about 100 others following a survey of unaided madrasas.“The 252 madrasas that have been served closure notices are devoid of minimum infrastructure. The 100-odd that have been issued show-cause will have to respond and and if their replies are found to be unsatisfactory, we will take action against them too. We want madrasa students to pursue modern, mainstream education and shine in life just like students from other schools,” said Kshudiram Tudu, minister-in-charge of the department.Malda leads the list of closures with around 44-45 madrasas while North Dinajpur is second with around 37, followed by 32-odd in South 24 Parganas and about 25 each in Murshidabad and Nadia.The action followed a field verification through the district administration of all madrasas, with particular focus on Khariji madrasas. The aim was to identify madrasas functioning without authorisation and ensure compliance with regulatory framework.Khariji madrasas are independent Islamic schools that operate without govt funding, formal recognition or regulatory control. They rely entirely on public donations and charitable trusts.Deviation from syllabus, lack of classroom space among issuesThe magistrates of all 22 districts and the Kolkata area submitted reports on madrasas functioning within their respective jurisdictions. Detailed information relating to registration status, management, student enrolment and identity, teaching staff, infrastructure and sources of funding were collected and scrutinised.The DMs reported that about 2,132 madrasas were functioning with proper registration/affiliation etc, while 2,396 were functioning without the required registration/affiliation from any govt or board. The department deputed dedicated inspection/investigation teams from the state level for re-verification of the reports received to ascertain that correctness of information furnished by the institutions corresponded with the actual position on the ground.The infrastructural lacunae at the madrasas included non-availability of classroom space, inadequate students or teachers, stark deviation from standard state school syllabus or administrative rules.According to a senior Nabanna official, state govt found that in a good number of Khariji madrasas, anti-India education was being imparted and innocent students were being brainwashed, that has prompted the survey exercise. articles.title: Three years before 9/11, CIA warned Clinton that Bin Laden wanted to strike India
articles.summary: India News: Three years before the 9/11 attacks shocked the United States, then-President Bill Clinton was warned by the CIA that Osama bin Laden intended to carr.
articles.body: Three years before the 9/11 attacks shocked the United States, then-President Bill Clinton was warned by the CIA that Osama bin Laden intended to carry out attacks in India, Pakistan, Uganda and possibly Nigeria.A newly declassified CIA warning dated August 28, 1998, said Bin Laden had survived US missile strikes in Afghanistan and retained a network of individuals and allied groups across at least 60 countries that could be used to mount attacks.The assessment specifically listed India and Pakistan, along with Egypt, the Arabian Peninsula – particularly Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Yemen – Uganda and possibly Nigeria, as countries where Bin Laden intended to conduct attacks.Bin Laden also viewed India as part of what he described as a “Crusader-Zionist-Hindu” conspiracy against the Islamic world, reflecting the ideological lens through which he framed India and its relationship with the US and Israel.The CIA said Bin Laden was also considering further attacks against the US and UK, although he had not indicated precise targets or timing.The assessment came weeks after the August 1998 bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, which killed more than 200 people and brought Bin Laden's organisation firmly into the sights of US counterterrorism agencies.The newly released document said Bin Laden’s infrastructure in North America, Europe and East Asia also lent credibility to reports that he could target US interests in those regions.The CIA assessment further noted that Bin Laden had authorised an associate to explore attacks in the US and that US officials had recently helped arrest Bin Laden operatives preparing attacks in Tirana and possibly Baku.The India reference is significant because it shows that the threat posed by Bin Laden’s network was being assessed as extending beyond the Middle East, Africa and the US well before the September 11 attacks.The August 1998 assessment was part of a series of intelligence warnings about Bin Laden that accumulated in the years before 9/11. articles.title: Rescuers search for over 100 people after Indonesian passenger ship sinks
articles.summary: Search and rescue ongoing after Virgo Transport 8, with 243 people on board, lost contact with its operator.
articles.body:
Rescuers are searching for more than 100 people from an Indonesian passenger ship that sank in the Java Sea after 115 others were evacuated, one of whom has died, authorities said.

The Virgo Transport 8, with 243 people on board, lost contact with its operator in the early hours of Sunday, according to Indonesia’s search and rescue agency.

It had sailed from Surabaya on the Indonesian island of Java on Saturday and was heading for Banjarmasin, a port city on Borneo.

Rescuers are searching for the remaining passengers and crew.

The ship encountered rough weather, said I Putu Sudayana, head of the local search-and-rescue office in Banjarmasin.

The ferry’s last known position was in the Java Sea, about 81 nautical miles (equivalent to about 150km) from Banjarmasin, the AFP news agency reported.

Rescue ships and a helicopter have been searching the area, where Sudayana said waves as high as 2.5 metres (8.2ft) have hampered the operation.

“It is extremely risky for vessels. Even our Basarnas vessel, which is 40 metres (131ft) long, is at great risk,” Sudayana told reporters, referring to the country’s search-and-rescue agency.

Al Jazeera’s Jessica Washington, reporting from Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, said authorities have yet to determine the cause of the sinking.

An investigation is under way, Washington added, with authorities examining factors including the weather and possible technical failures.

People in Indonesia, an archipelago of ‌17,000 islands, rely on ferries as a key mode of transport, with sea routes more affordable and readily available than ‌air ‌travel.

Last month, a fire on a ferry sailing between Bali and Lombok killed one person and left five missing. In July, a ferry carrying more than 70 people sank near Selayar Island, south of Sulawesi.

articles.title: Swedes vote in election that could usher far right into government
articles.summary: Swedes vote in an election on Sunday that will either bring a far-right party into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long ⁠been known for.
articles.body: STOCKHOLM — Swedes vote in an election on Sunday that will either bring a far-right party into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long ⁠been known for. Sweden’s centre-left opposition holds a narrow lead over the ruling right-wing bloc ahead of a September 13 election for parliament, pointing to a likely change of government, several opinion polls have shown this week. But Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, who has trailed in opinion polls throughout his four years in office, has been catching up in the final weeks of campaigning, with rival Magdalena Andersson and her Social Democrats losing ground. Supporters of the right-wing bloc ⁠say its policies have helped curb gang violence and cut immigration dramatically, ​and that ⁠a victory would amount to a public endorsement of that approach and more in the same vein in the years ahead. “We can unify parties, voters and issues into joint action. That’s why we get things done,” Kristersson, who has ⁠pledged to bring the far-right Sweden Democrats into government if his bloc wins, told reporters in parliament this week. Critics counter that ​the agenda ⁠is undermining civil liberties while forcing immigrants to conform ‌more closely to Swedish cultural norms or leave the country, urged on by both carrot and stick. “We’ve become a harder society, a quieter society, but also a poorer society as we’ve had growth far below our potential and where households see their pay checks buy ‌less and less,” Andersson told Reuters. “Our country has based its strength on sharing ‌in each other’s achievements and that we stick together when things are hard.” Europe trends to far right Polling stations in the EU member state of 10 million people, which joined NATO after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, open at 8 a.m. (2 a.m. ET) with exit polls due soon after they close at 8 p.m. (2 p.m. ET) Electoral success ⁠for the Sweden Democrats would be welcomed by Europe’s rising far-right parties, boosted by a significant win in a German state election this month by the anti-immigrant Alternative for Germany. The right has already agreed to form a four-party government led by Kristersson if they win, while Andersson’s path to power is more uncertain. The election could ultimately be decided by whether the Liberals surpass the 4% threshold to win seats in parliament, bolstering a right wing that includes Moderates, Christian Democrats and, since being invited by Kristersson earlier this year, Sweden Democrats. Led by veteran party leader Jimmie Akesson, the Sweden Democrats have already spent four years propping up Kristersson’s minority government in parliament, building credibility with the ‌broader right-wing bloc. Meanwhile, the rival blocs have converged on several voter priorities, including support for Ukraine, military rearmament and relief ​for households hit by the cost-of-living crisis. While the opposition Social Democrats, Greens, Left Party and Centre Party broadly agree ‌on the need for higher welfare and public spending, divisions ⁠persist on many issues, including immigration, where Andersson’s party wants a more restrictive line than some of its would-be partners. They are ⁠also at odds over issues including a tax on billionaires and building new nuclear reactors, while the Centre refuses to support a government that includes the Left Party, increasing ‌the challenge Andersson would face to ​form a cabinet. Luring the Christian Democrats to switch camps to create ‌a centrist government is favoured by the Centre Party but ​so far looks a distant prospect.

articles.title: Reform's £72m donations 'entirely in line with law', Jenrick says
articles.summary: The government is trying to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats.
articles.body:
Robert Jenrick has said Reform UK believed that £72m in donations it has received from two cryptocurrency billionaires were "entirely in line with the law".

The party's economic spokesman told the BBC that he did not expect that it will have to return any of the money from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British and have spent time living overseas.

The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats, including a £100,000 cap backdated to 25 March.

"These two donations are entirely in line with the law as it is and, as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future," Jenrick said.

Jenrick also told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "It might be that [Housing Secretary] Angela Rayner or the government keep trying to change the law to make it even harder for people to donate to Reform, nothing would surprise me.

"But, as it stands, we believe these are entirely in line with the law."

BBC News has been told that both Delo and Harborne have returned to the UK. Delo is understood to have been back in the country since last year.

Jenrick said Delo had returned to the UK "in part so that he can comply with the changes to the law".

As well as limiting how much British citizens can donate to political parties from overseas, the government has proposed limiting how much those who move back to the UK can give to £100,000 in the remainder of the calendar year and the following calendar year after they return.

Who is Reform donor and crypto billionaire Ben Delo?

Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

The measures were added to the Representation of the People Bill after they were approved by MPs this month. The bill still needs to be scrutinised in the House of Lords.

Rayner, who also appeared on the programme, said the changes proposed by the government were "directly as a result" of a review by former top civil servant Philip Rycroft , published on 25 March.

Rayner said: "We said that because of the intention of the legislation and the recommendations, which we accepted, was known in the public domain that it would be retrospective to that date.

"That legislation is going through Parliament at the moment and we've also written to the Electoral Commission, which is an independent body, to see what further measures we need to take to protect our democracy."

There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties.

The government has previously said it was "determined to tackle" the issue of "mega-donors", and has established a new taskforce to do this.

It did not support calls from some MPs for a cap but Rayner left the door open to the possibility of further restrictions.

"It's not as simple as we're saying we won't put a cap [on donations], it's a question of making sure that the task and finish group look at how we implement this."

Rayner said the aim would be to "protect our democracy in the spirit of individuals not being able to overpower and buy their way into democracy at the expense of those people that are at the ballot box".

She would not be drawn on whether the proposed changes would apply to Delo and Harborne, saying: "I don't know the individual circumstances of those donors."

Jenrick said Delo and Harborne - who each gave £36m to the party in two days and now share the record for the largest ever donation given to a UK political party - were "not buying anything, they simply support our agenda".

Both men had already donated millions of pounds to Reform ahead of the announcement of their latest contributions.

The Times reported in June that Harborne, who has been based in Thailand, had registered to vote in the UK, while Delo had told the Telegraph in April that he was moving back from Hong Kong.

Harborne wrote in the Telegraph on Saturday that Reform was a "start-up party" that lacked "the benefit of hundreds of years of patronage". Delo had written in the newspaper the day prior that he wanted to enable Reform to put up a "fair fight at the next election.

Delo was pardoned by US President Donald Trump last year over a breach of anti-money laundering laws at his crypto trading platform, BitMex, to which he had pleaded guilty in 2022.
